title: Contributions of auditory and somatosensory feedback to vocal motor control
venue: Journal of Speech, Language, and Hearing Research
excerpt:
To better define the contributions of somatosensory
and auditory feedback in vocal motor control, a laryngeal
perturbation experiment was conducted with and without
masking of auditory feedback.
citation: Smith, D.J., Stepp, C., Guenther, F. H., & Kearney, E. (2020). Contributions of auditory and somatosensory feedback to vocal motor control. Journal of Speech, Language, and Hearing Research, 63(7), 2039-2053. https://doi.org/10.1044/2020_JSLHR-19-00296

title: Chunking of phonological units in speech sequencing
excerpt: We found that performance improvements induration from practicing syllables with non-native consonant clusters largely generalized to new syllables thatcontained those clusters. Practicing the whole syllable, however, resulted in larger performance gains in errorrates compared to practicing just the consonant clusters.
citation: Segawa, J., Masapollo, M., Tong, M,. Smith, D. J., Guenther, F. H. (2019). Chunking of phonological units in speech sequencing. Brain and Language, 195(May), 104636. https://10.1016/j.bandl.2019.05.001

title: Comparison of steady-state visual and somatosensory evoked potentials for brain-computer interface control
venue: 2014 36th Annual Internal Conference of the IEEE in Engineering in Medicine and Biology Society
excerpt: Here, we compare the neural signals elicited by SSSEP to those elicited by SSVEP in naïve BCI users towards evaluating the feasibility of SSSEP-based control of an EEG BCI.
citation: Smith, D.J., Varghese, L. A., Stepp, C. E., & Guenther, F. H. (2014). Comparison of steady-state visual and somatosensory evoked potentials for brain-computer interface control. 2014 36th Annual International Conference of the IEEE Engineering in Medicine and Biology Society, 1234-1237, https://10.1109/EMBC.2014.6943820
